articles.title: Weekly Commentary (31 July 2026)
articles.claim_summary: Major technology hyperscalers are maintaining intact capital expenditure plans despite macroeconomic headwinds, while China has achieved a technological breakthrough in DUV lithography. Simultaneously, both the Federal Reserve (FOMC) and the Bank of Japan (BOJ) have adopted hawkish holds on interest rates, creating a distinct environment for tech and global equity investors.

articles.title: BOJ’s Hawkish Hold: Another 2026 Hike Is Still on the Table
articles.claim_summary: The Bank of Japan maintained its policy interest rate in a hawkish hold, projecting core inflation at or above 2% through its entire forecast horizon with upside price risks. Despite an apparent downgrade to near-term inflation caused by temporary government subsidies, the central bank's underlying policy outlook remains unchanged, keeping additional rate hikes through 2026 on the table.

findings.title: Market consensus of Bank of Japan's terminal rate at 2% is a bit too ambitious: Strategist - CNBC
findings.reason: J.P. Morgan Asset Management's strategist confirms expectations that the Bank of Japan will 'hike interest rate in the September meeting and keeps hiking every 6 months,' supporting that additional rate hikes remain on the table.

articles.title: Malaysia Sector Outlook: Plantation - Positive Catalysts Largely Priced In; Neutral View
articles.claim_summary: NEUTRAL stance on the Malaysian plantation sector: the 2026 CPO price rally (driven by elevated crude oil amid the US-Iran conflict and Indonesia's B50 biodiesel mandate) is seen as largely priced in already. CPO is expected to stay range-bound in 2026, with a floor near RM4,000/tonne from Indonesia's B50 diverting 3-4 million tonnes of palm oil from exports, but capped upside from record Brazilian soybean production compressing the palm-soy spread. Structural constraints include 32% of Malaysian palm trees aged above 19 years and low replanting rates limiting production growth.

findings.title: CPO prices to stay firm above RM4,600 in September on tightening supply and geopolitical disruptions — MPOC - The Edge Malaysia
findings.reason: The MPOC reports that CPO prices are supported by 'Indonesia’s palm oil demand for B50 biodiesel blending' as well as geopolitical disruptions, while Malaysian production in July marked the fifth consecutive month of year-on-year decline.

articles.title: Malaysia Sector Outlook: Construction - Year of Execution
articles.claim_summary: 2026 is the Malaysian construction sector's "Execution Year": record 2025 contract awards (RM202.5 billion) are expected to translate into peak earnings delivery for major contractors. Budget 2026 development expenditure eases to RM81 billion (from RM86 billion in 2025), but the 13th Malaysia Plan maintains a RM430 billion total allocation through 2030, sustaining infrastructure commitment. Data centres remain the key structural growth driver alongside transport, industrial parks and renewable energy projects; margin risks from steel/cement/labour inflation are seen as manageable given strong order books.

findings.title: Zecon seeks partners for its 3,000-acre Sarawak green tech park - The Edge Malaysia
findings.reason: Sarawak-based construction and engineering group Zecon is actively developing a 3,000-acre green tech park combining solar power generation, data centres, and industrial manufacturing facilities.

articles.title: Top & Bottom Bond Funds 2Q26: Bond Markets Rebound, but Rate Risks Remain

findings.title: Short-dated debt still offers value amid global bond rout, says UBS. Here's why - CNBC
findings.reason: UBS analysts note that with the long end of the yield curve exposed to fiscal and inflation uncertainty, they 'continue to see short- and medium-maturity quality bonds as attractive' because higher yields offer a cushion against further rate hikes.
